summary: The retrieved content provides a comprehensive guide to implementing a calendar popup system in web applications using JavaScript. It covers various aspects including the construction of calendar objects, customization of appearance through CSS, navigation through months, quarters, and years, and interaction with form inputs for date selection.
purpose: The primary purpose of the retrieved content is to offer a set of JavaScript functions and methodologies to create a flexible and customizable calendar popup interface. This can be integrated into web applications to enhance user interaction with date selections.

workflows.name: Calendar Popup Interaction
steps: Set display preferences such as month names, abbreviations, and CSS styles.
Bind the calendar to a text input field for date selection.
Use methods like showCalendar() and hideCalendar() to control the popup's display.

business_rules: The popup can be positioned relative to an anchor element.
The calendar supports different types of displays: date, month, quarter, and year.
Navigation can be shown as dropdowns or links for year and month selections.
validations: Function isDate() checks the validity of a date string against a given format.
compareDates() compares two date strings to determine which is earlier.
calculations: Leap year determination for accurate February date handling.
Calculations for next and previous months and years for navigation.
conditions: Conditional display based on the current date and set preferences for disabled dates.
system_behavior: Automatic hiding of the calendar when clicking outside if autoHide is enabled.
Popup window reflects changes made to the contents dynamically using refresh().
exceptions: Errors shown if unsupported display types or invalid formats are used.
Alerts for unhandled date selections if return functions are undefined.
